intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Prague's Old Town Square, witness the iconic medieval Astronomical Clock strike the hour with its parade of apostles, and explore the Gothic Týn Church. Join a free walking tour to uncover centuries of Bohemian history from local guides.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in the grandeur of one of Europe's largest thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Enjoy indoor and outdoor pools fed by natural hot springs beneath the city. A quintessential Budapest ritual blending history, wellness, and local culture all in one iconic setting.

experiences.name: Prague Local Food Market & Czech Cuisine Tasting
experiences.description: Visit the Náplavka Farmers' Market along the Vltava riverbank and sample authentic Czech street food including svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce), trdelník pastry, and locally brewed craft beer. Chat with vendors and immerse yourself in the everyday food culture of Prague locals.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl in the Jewish Quarter
experiences.description: Explore the legendary ruin bars of Budapest's historic Jewish Quarter, starting with the iconic Szimpla Kert — a crumbling pre-war building transformed into a vibrant cultural hub. Sip Hungarian pálinka (fruit brandy) and craft beers while absorbing the eclectic art, live music, and bohemian atmosphere unique to Budapest nightlife.

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex & Golden Lane Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the largest ancient castle complex in the world, perched dramatically above the Vltava River. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the charming Golden Lane — a row of tiny colorful houses once inhabited by castle guards and alchemists. Sweeping panoramic views of Prague's red rooftops are included at no extra cost.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at 13:00, clear customs, and take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky for ~60 CZK (~€2.50), then walk or take tram to your hotel in Staré Město. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed self-guided walk through Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) — admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj), Týn Church, and the medieval architecture. Free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across Charles Bridge (Karlův most) at dusk for stunning views of Prague Castle and the Vltava River. Enjoy the street musicians and artists. Then explore the narrow cobblestone lanes of Malá Strana (Lesser Town) just across the bridge.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or trdelník (chimney cake) from a street stall near Old Town Square for ~80–120 CZK (~€3–5).
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved Czech pub in Staré Město offering fresh Pilsner Urquell on tap and classic Czech dishes like goulash and roast pork. Budget ~200–300 CZK (~€8–12) per person.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour public transport pass for 120 CZK (~€5) at the airport — it covers buses, trams, and metro. Download the PID Lítačka app for easy navigation. September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C), so pack a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle in the world. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Buy a combined ticket (Circuit B) for ~250 CZK (~€10). Arrive early (9:00) to beat crowds. Walk up Nerudova Street for a scenic approach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into Malá Strana and visit the baroque Wallenstein Garden (free entry) and St. Nicholas Church. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) from the outside — admire the Old Jewish Cemetery and synagogue facades. Full interior entry is expensive (~550 CZK), so opt for the exterior and the free Old Jewish Cemetery view from the gate if on a tight budget.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood by tram for a more local, less touristy evening. Walk up to Žižkov TV Tower and see the famous crawling baby sculptures (free, exterior). Enjoy craft beer at a local pivnice (pub).

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry (koláč or rohlík) and coffee at Kavárna Místo or any local bakery near Old Town — ~60–80 CZK (~€2.50–3).
meals.lunch: Eat at a Czech canteen-style restaurant (jídelna) near Malá Strana — try svíčková or roast duck with dumplings for ~120–160 CZK (~€5–6.50). Try U Kocoura on Nerudova Street.
meals.dinner: Hospůdka Na Výšince in Žižkov — a classic local pub with hearty Czech food and cheap beer (~0.5L Pilsner for ~40 CZK). Full meal under 200 CZK (~€8).

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is a steep uphill walk — wear comfortable shoes. The castle grounds are free to enter; only the interior buildings require tickets. Trams 22 and 23 are your best friends for getting around Prague's hills.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad — the lesser-known but equally stunning hilltop fortress with panoramic views of Prague and the Vltava. Explore the Vyšehrad Cemetery (burial place of Czech legends like Dvořák and Smetana), the Romanesque Rotunda of St. Martin, and the Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul. Entry to grounds is free; basilica ~50 CZK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nusle Valley and walk along the riverbank back toward the city center. Visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square — recently renovated, entry ~200 CZK (~€8). Stroll Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) — a historic boulevard, site of the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague has incredibly affordable evening concerts in historic churches and halls. Check GoOut.cz or Ticketportal for concerts at St. James Basilica or Municipal House for ~200–400 CZK (~€8–16). Alternatively, enjoy free live jazz at many Old Town bars.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy or a local café near the hotel — order a Czech open-faced sandwich (obložený chlebíček) and coffee for ~100 CZK (~€4).
meals.lunch: Picnic in Vyšehrad park — pick up bread, local cheese (Olomoucké tvarůžky), and fruit from an Albert supermarket for ~80–100 CZK (~€3–4). Eat with a view of the Vltava.
meals.dinner: Kantýna in Nové Město — a butcher-style restaurant known for excellent quality Czech meat dishes at surprisingly affordable prices. Expect ~250–350 CZK (~€10–14) per person including a beer.

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is easily reached by Metro C (red line) to Vyšehrad station. This is a quieter, more authentic side of Prague that most tourists miss. The cemetery is genuinely moving and historically rich.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at the Farmers' Market at Náměstí Míru (Vinohrady) — one of Prague's best local markets, open Fridays. Sample local produce, cheeses, cured meats, and homemade pastries. Then explore the beautiful Art Nouveau architecture of Vinohrady neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Budapest by RegioJet or FlixBus — book in advance for fares as low as €10–15. The journey takes approximately 6.5–7 hours by bus or ~7 hours by train. Depart around 13:00–14:00 from Florenc Bus Station (reachable by metro). Arrive in Budapest in the early evening. Check into your Budapest accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest and take a short orientation walk along the Danube Embankment near your accommodation. See the illuminated Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) and Parliament Building from the Pest side — absolutely stunning at night and completely free.

meals.breakfast: Fresh market breakfast at Náměstí Míru Farmers' Market — try homemade pastries and a local coffee for ~100–120 CZK (~€4–5).
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the bus ride — grab a baguette sandwich and snacks from a Prague supermarket or deli before departure (~80–100 CZK / ~€3–4).
meals.dinner: Upon arrival in Budapest, head to the Great Market Hall area or Belváros (Inner City) for a quick and cheap Hungarian meal. Try lángos (deep-fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor for ~600–800 HUF (~€1.50–2).

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest bus tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance on RegioJet.com for the best prices. Buses are comfortable with WiFi and power outlets. Alternatively, a night train exists but is pricier. Exchange some Czech Koruna (CZK) back to euros or get Hungarian Forints (HUF) upon arrival — Budapest uses HUF.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle District (Budavári Palota) — take the historic funicular (Budavári Sikló) up Castle Hill for ~1,400 HUF (~€3.50) or walk up for free. Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) exterior and Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — the bastion's lower terrace is free; upper towers cost ~1,500 HUF (~€4). Enjoy panoramic views over the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Castle Hill and cross the iconic Chain Bridge on foot. Explore the Inner City (Belváros) of Pest — stroll Váci Street and the surrounding pedestrian zone. Visit the stunning St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István-bazilika) — entry is free, though a donation of ~200 HUF is suggested. Climb the dome for panoramic views (~800 HUF / ~€2).
day_by_day.evening: Experience a Budapest ruin bar (romkocsma) — head to the Jewish Quarter (VII. District) and visit the legendary Szimpla Kert, the original ruin bar. It's quirky, artistic, and has affordable drinks (~700–1,000 HUF / ~€1.80–2.50 per beer). Also walk past the Great Synagogue (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest in Europe — beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh lángos or a kifli (Hungarian crescent roll) with butter and jam from a local pékség (bakery) near your accommodation — ~300–500 HUF (~€0.80–1.30).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) on Fővám tér — a Budapest institution. Try goulash soup (gulyásleves) or stuffed cabbage (töltött káposzta) at the food stalls on the upper floor for ~1,500–2,000 HUF (~€4–5).
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food Court in the Jewish Quarter — an outdoor street food park next to Szimpla Kert with multiple vendors offering Hungarian and international food. Budget ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~€4–6.50) for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Budapest public transport (BKK) is excellent and affordable — buy a 24-hour pass for ~2,500 HUF (~€6.50) or a 72-hour pass for ~5,000 HUF (~€13). The Saturday Great Market Hall is very busy — arrive before 10:30 to avoid the biggest crowds. Szimpla Kert also hosts a Sunday farmers' market.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — one of Budapest's most iconic landmarks, completely free. Explore the Millennium Monument and the two flanking art museums. Then walk through City Park (Városliget) — a beautiful green space with the fairy-tale Vajdahunyad Castle (exterior free) and the famous Széchenyi Thermal Bath nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi gyógyfürdő) — one of Europe's largest and most beautiful thermal bath complexes. A weekend cabin ticket costs ~8,500–9,500 HUF (~€22–25), which is a splurge but a quintessential Budapest experience worth budgeting for. Spend 2–3 hours relaxing in the outdoor and indoor pools.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take the metro to the Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand boulevard, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Stroll toward the Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház) — admire the stunning Neo-Renaissance facade. If budget allows, standing tickets for opera performances can be as low as ~1,000–3,000 HUF (~€2.50–8). Otherwise, enjoy the free exterior and the lively street scene.

meals.breakfast: Szimpla Farmers' Market (Sunday morning at Szimpla Kert, 9:00–14:00) — grab fresh local produce, homemade jams, artisan bread, and coffee in a unique ruin bar setting. Budget ~500–800 HUF (~€1.30–2) for a light breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the Sunday market and eat in City Park near Vajdahunyad Castle — a very local and relaxing experience.
meals.dinner: Bors GasztroBar in the Jewish Quarter — a legendary tiny spot famous for creative soups and baguette sandwiches. Extremely popular with locals. A filling meal costs ~1,500–2,000 HUF (~€4–5). Arrive early as lines form quickly.

day_by_day.notes: The thermal bath is the one bigger expense of the trip but is deeply embedded in Hungarian culture — it's worth it. Book online in advance to save time and sometimes money. September is a great month for outdoor pools as the weather is still warm enough.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side — enjoy views of Buda Castle, Gellért Hill, and the bridges. Visit the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — a deeply moving Holocaust monument, free to visit. Then walk to the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) for exterior photos — one of the world's most beautiful parliamentary buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the best panoramic views of Budapest — completely free. The hike takes about 20–30 minutes. Visit the Citadella fortress at the top and the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor). Descend to the Gellért Thermal Bath area and explore the elegant Gellért Hotel facade without paying for entry.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Belváros and Ferencváros (IX. District) neighborhoods — increasingly hip areas with local bars, street art, and affordable restaurants. Visit the Hold Street Market (Hold utcai vásárcsarnok) area in the evening for a local atmosphere. End the night with a farewell Budapest cocktail or palinka (Hungarian fruit brandy) at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square — a historic Budapest institution. A coffee and pastry here is a cultural experience (~1,500–2,000 HUF / ~€4–5), slightly above budget but worth it once for the atmosphere.
meals.lunch: Főzelékfaló Ételbár — a local chain specializing in főzelék (Hungarian vegetable stew/thick soup), a traditional and very cheap Hungarian staple. Full meal ~1,200–1,800 HUF (~€3–4.50).
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant on Liszt Ferenc Square — retro-styled restaurant serving updated Hungarian classics at reasonable prices. Main dishes ~3,500–5,000 HUF (~€9–13). Liszt Ferenc Square itself is a lively pedestrian area perfect for a final Budapest evening.

day_by_day.notes: The Shoes on the Danube memorial is most impactful in the early morning or evening light — plan your walk accordingly. Gellért Hill can be slippery after rain, so wear good shoes. Palinka is very strong (40–70% ABV) — try a small tasting glass at a bar for ~500–800 HUF (~€1.30–2).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — revisit a favorite spot or explore any missed areas. Consider visiting the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum) — excellent coverage of Hungarian history from prehistoric times to the present, entry ~1,600 HUF (~€4). Alternatively, browse the antique and flea market at Ecseri Piac if it fits your departure schedule (open Mon–Fri 8:00–16:00, Sat until 15:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — head to Budapest Keleti, Kelenföldi, or Budapest Airport. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport is reachable by Bus 100E from Deák Ferenc tér for ~900 HUF (~€2.30) — the most budget-friendly airport transfer. Allow 45–60 minutes travel time plus check-in time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure / travel home. Reflect on an incredible 8 days of history, culture, stunning architecture, thermal baths, craft beer, and incredible food across two of Central Europe's most beautiful capitals.

meals.breakfast: One last Hungarian breakfast — stop at a local pékség (bakery) for fresh pogácsa (savory scones), a kifli, and a strong espresso. ~400–600 HUF (~€1–1.50).
meals.lunch: Quick and filling meal before departure — try a gyros or kebab from one of the many affordable spots near Keleti Station (~1,500 HUF / ~€4), or grab a lángos from a street vendor for a final taste of Budapest.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or pack snacks from a local supermarket (Spar, Aldi, or Tesco) before heading to the airport for the most budget-friendly option.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for the full 8 days (excluding flights and accommodation): Transport Prague (3 days pass) ~360 CZK, Prague–Budapest bus ~€12, Budapest transport (72hr pass) ~€13, food ~€8–15/day, attractions ~€20–30 total. Estimated total spending money: €120–180 for the full trip. Always carry some local cash as many local spots in both cities prefer cash. Both cities are extremely safe for tourists but keep an eye on pickpockets in crowded tourist areas.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transit from airport to hotel in Staré Město via Airport Express bus to Náměstí Republiky (~35 min, ~60 CZK). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle neighborhood orientation walk through Staré Město (Old Town). Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge, admire the Baroque statues, and soak in your first views of the Vltava River and Prague Castle skyline. Wander through Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the twin-spired Týn Church — all within easy walking distance of your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric lanes of Josefov (Jewish Quarter) at dusk for a scenic evening walk. Head back to Old Town Square to see it lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or skip — arrival day.
meals.lunch: Café Louvre-style stop near the hotel — try Café Savoy or a local bakery for open-faced chlebíčky sandwiches (~150–200 CZK).
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá Street, near Old Town) — a beloved Czech gastropub serving traditional svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell. Budget ~350–500 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on getting your bearings rather than packing in too many sights. Exchange some cash to CZK at the airport or use a fee-free ATM in Old Town.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Prague Castle complex (Pražský hrad) — one of the largest castle complexes in the world. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Take tram No. 22 from Náměstí Republiky up the hill or walk up via Nerudova Street for scenic views. Allow 2.5–3 hours. Book tickets online in advance (~250–350 CZK for the standard circuit).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — explore the charming baroque district below the castle. Visit the ornate St. Nicholas Church (free exterior, ~70 CZK interior). Browse the boutique shops and galleries along Nerudova and Thunovská streets. Cross back over Charles Bridge and visit the Old Town Bridge Tower for panoramic views (~100 CZK).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague has nightly performances in historic venues. Check out concerts at the Municipal House (Obecní dům) or a church concert near Old Town Square (~400–800 CZK). Book same-day at the venue or via GoOut.net.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or nearby — try Café Nona or Eska (Holešovice-adjacent) for a modern Czech breakfast (~150–200 CZK).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from the Havelské tržiště (Havel's Market) near Old Town — grab fresh fruit, trdelník, and local cheeses (~100–150 CZK).
meals.dinner: Kolkovna Olympia in Malá Strana — hearty Czech classics like roast duck with red cabbage and bread dumplings in a lively beer hall setting (~350–500 CZK per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — Prague Castle involves significant uphill walking and cobblestones. September weather is typically mild (15–22°C), so a light jacket is recommended for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — explore the six historic synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery, one of Europe's oldest and most atmospheric. The combined ticket covers the Pinkas, Maisel, Spanish, and Klaus Synagogues plus the cemetery (~350 CZK). Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods via tram for a taste of local Prague life away from tourists. Visit the Žižkov Television Tower (unique brutalist landmark with David Černý's crawling baby sculptures) and enjoy panoramic views from the observation deck (~230 CZK). Browse the independent cafés and vintage shops along Mánesova and Blanická streets in Vinohrady.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a Prague food and beer tasting experience. Join a 2-hour guided street food tour of Old Town and New Town (~600–800 CZK) or self-guide through Dlouhá Street's restaurant strip.

meals.breakfast: Café Imperial (Na Příkopě, 15-min walk) — a stunning Art Nouveau café famous for its mosaic-tiled interior and excellent breakfasts (~200–300 CZK).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Žižkov at Pivnice u Sadu — a classic local pub with cheap Czech lunch specials (polední menu ~150–180 CZK including soup and main).
meals.dinner: Manifesto Market (seasonal container market, check if open in Sept) or Naše maso butcher deli on Dlouhá — artisan Czech charcuterie and craft beer (~250–400 CZK).

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter is closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays — Wednesday is a perfect day to visit. Buy Josefov tickets online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (1.5 hours from Prague by direct train, ~120 CZK each way). Visit the hauntingly beautiful Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) — decorated with the bones of 40,000+ people. Then explore the stunning UNESCO-listed St. Barbara's Cathedral and the medieval silver-mining town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kutná Hora's historic center — visit the Italian Court (Vlašský dvůr), former royal mint, and the Gothic Stone Fountain. Head back to Prague by late afternoon (trains run hourly). Arrive back in Old Town by 17:00–18:00.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Prague — explore Náplavka (riverside embankment) for a sunset stroll along the Vltava. In September, the Náplavka farmers' market may still be running on Fridays. Enjoy a riverside beer at one of the floating bars.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at your hotel or grab a coffee and pastry to go before catching the morning train.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora — Restaurace Donna or V Ruthardce near St. Barbara's Cathedral. Traditional Czech lunch for ~200–300 CZK.
meals.dinner: Pasta Fresca or Café de Paris near Old Town — lighter European dinner after a long day out (~300–450 CZK per person).

day_by_day.notes: Trains from Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Station) to Kutná Hora run regularly — aim for the 08:30 or 09:00 departure to maximize time. The Bone Church is a 15-min walk or short bus from Kutná Hora train station.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Prague to Budapest by Regiojet or Czech Railways train (approx. 7 hours, ~€20–35 booked in advance). Depart Praha hlavní nádraží around 08:00–09:00. The scenic route passes through the Czech and Slovak countryside — enjoy the views and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest Keleti Station around 15:00–16:00. Check into your Budapest accommodation (pre-booked). Take a short walk to get oriented in your neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Budapest — head to the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) if still open (closes ~18:00 on Saturdays) or stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side for stunning views of Buda Castle and Chain Bridge illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near Prague hotel or at the station before departure — bakery items or a station café (~100–150 CZK).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or buy food on the Regiojet train (they have a bistro car with decent snacks and meals, ~€5–10).
meals.dinner: Belvárosi Lugas — a beloved traditional Hungarian restaurant near the center. Try goulash soup (gulyásleves) and chicken paprikash (csirkepaprikás) for your first authentic Hungarian meal (~3,500–5,000 HUF per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Prague–Budapest train well in advance on regiojet.com or cd.cz for best prices. Regiojet offers comfortable seats with free Wi-Fi and snack service. Have some Hungarian Forints (HUF) ready upon arrival — exchange at the airport or use ATMs (avoid exchange booths at Keleti Station).

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~1,400 HUF round trip) from Clark Ádám Square up to the castle district. Visit the Royal Palace (home to the Hungarian National Gallery — free on some days), the Fishermen's Bastion (Halászbástya) for sweeping panoramic views of the Danube and Pest, and the Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom, ~2,000 HUF). Allow 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot back to Pest — a classic Budapest experience. Explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées), a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard lined with neo-Renaissance mansions. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House exterior and, if time allows, take a 45-minute guided interior tour (~3,000 HUF).
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Hungarian thermal bath — visit Széchenyi Baths in City Park (one of Europe's largest, ~7,200 HUF entry). The Saturday night 'sparty' (spa party) is famous but crowded — opt for a quieter Sunday evening soak instead. Open until 22:00.

meals.breakfast: New York Café breakfast — Budapest's most opulent café (splurge-worthy at ~4,000–6,000 HUF) or a lighter option at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square (~2,000–3,000 HUF).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Fishermen's Bastion — Halászbástya Restaurant has great views but can be pricey; alternatively, grab a lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese, ~800–1,200 HUF) from a street vendor at the castle.
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant on Liszt Ferenc Square — retro-communist-chic design serving modern Hungarian classics at mid-range prices (~3,500–5,500 HUF per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit and towel for the thermal baths (or rent on-site for ~1,000–1,500 HUF). Széchenyi is in City Park — easily reached by Metro Line M1 (the historic 'little yellow metro', Europe's oldest continental subway).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings, best seen from the Danube or up close on Kossuth Square. Book an English guided tour in advance (~8,000 HUF for non-EU citizens, ~4,000 HUF for EU citizens). Tours run every hour. Afterward, walk to the nearby Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — a moving Holocaust memorial of iron shoes on the riverbank.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world. The complex includes a Jewish museum and the haunting Heroes' Temple and Memorial Garden (~5,000 HUF). Then wander through the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — Budapest's ruin bar district. See Gozsdu Udvar (a series of interconnected courtyards) and browse the independent shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Ruin bar experience in the Jewish Quarter — start at Szimpla Kert, Budapest's original and most famous ruin bar, for drinks in a wonderfully eclectic multi-room setting. Then explore neighboring bars like Instant-Fogas or Mazel Tov for a lively but authentic local evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local pékség (bakery) near your accommodation — try a kifli (crescent roll) or pogácsa (savory scone) with coffee (~500–800 HUF).
meals.lunch: Karavan Street Food Court next to Szimpla Kert — outdoor street food market with Hungarian and international options (~1,500–2,500 HUF).
meals.dinner: Kőleves (Stone Soup) Restaurant in the Jewish Quarter — a beloved neighborhood bistro with excellent Jewish-Hungarian fusion dishes and vegetarian options (~3,000–4,500 HUF per person).

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be pre-booked at jegymester.hu. Arrive 15 minutes early. The Jewish Quarter ruin bars are busiest after 21:00 on weekdays — perfect for a Monday evening since it won't be as crowded as weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit the Budapest Central Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) for a proper exploration and souvenir shopping. The ground floor has fresh produce, Hungarian salami (Pick Salami), paprika, and Tokaji wine. The upper floor has folk crafts, embroidery, and gifts. Budget ~1–2 hours and pick up edible souvenirs (~2,000–5,000 HUF depending on purchases). Then take a final stroll along the Danube Promenade for last views of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight/train: if time allows, visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) in Heroes' Square (~3,200 HUF) or simply relax in a traditional kávéház (coffee house) like Centrál Kávéház for a slow farewell coffee. Head to the airport or station — Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport is ~30 min by Airport Shuttle (~2,000 HUF) or Metro + bus (~900 HUF).
day_by_day.evening: Departure or overnight travel.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast at Belvárosi Piac café near the market or inside the market hall itself — fresh langos or a hearty egg dish (~1,000–1,500 HUF).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the market or airport — Vapiano or a quick Hungarian stand (~1,500–2,500 HUF).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight — or if departing late, a farewell dinner at Costes Downtown (splurge option, Budapest's Michelin-starred restaurant, ~15,000–20,000 HUF) or a casual final meal at Borkonyha Winekitchen (~6,000–9,000 HUF).

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and security. Budapest Airport has good duty-free shopping for last-minute Hungarian wine and Unicum (herbal liqueur) purchases. This wraps up a beautifully balanced 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most historic and culturally rich capitals.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury chauffeur service to your boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most), admire the 30 Baroque statues, and soak in your first views of the Vltava River. Continue into the Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the twin-spired Týn Church. Keep the pace leisurely — this is your arrival day.
day_by_day.evening: Evening aperitif at a rooftop bar overlooking the Old Town rooftops, then a welcome dinner at a celebrated Czech fine-dining restaurant. Explore the illuminated Old Town Square after dinner for a magical first impression of Prague by night.

meals.breakfast: Skipped — in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel or a quick stop at Café Savoy near the river for elegant open-faced sandwiches and Czech pastries
meals.dinner: Field by Radek Kašpárek (Michelin-starred) — contemporary Czech tasting menu featuring seasonal local ingredients, paired with curated Czech natural wines

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer before arrival. Ask the hotel concierge to book Field restaurant in advance as it fills up quickly. September in Prague is mild (15–22°C), ideal for evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) experience — the largest ancient castle in the world. Hire a private licensed guide for a 2-hour deep-dive tour covering St. Vitus Cathedral (stunning Gothic interior and royal tombs), the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) and explore the ornate Baroque Wallenstein Garden. Visit the Church of St. Nicholas, one of Central Europe's finest Baroque churches. Browse the boutique antique shops and art galleries along Nerudova Street. Return to the hotel for a rest before evening.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is renowned for chamber performances in historic venues. Choose a Mozart or Dvořák program held inside a Baroque palace or church. Follow with a late dinner in Malá Strana.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Café Louvre — a grand Art Nouveau café established in 1902, beloved by Kafka and Einstein, serving eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Hergetova Cihelna — riverside terrace restaurant in Malá Strana with panoramic Charles Bridge views; try the duck confit or beef tartare
meals.dinner: Augustine Restaurant at the Augustine Hotel — elegant setting in a 13th-century monastery, serving refined Czech and European cuisine with an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the private castle guide the night before through the hotel concierge. The castle complex requires 3–4 hours minimum. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestones. Concert tickets can be arranged via the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish heritage sites in Europe. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the hauntingly beautiful Pinkas Synagogue (memorial to Holocaust victims), the Spanish Synagogue (stunning Moorish interior), and the Maisel Synagogue. A private guide adds extraordinary depth to the experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mucha Museum to explore the Art Nouveau masterworks of Alphonse Mucha. Then head to the Municipal House (Obecní dům) for a guided interior tour of its magnificent Art Nouveau rooms. Stop into the opulent Café Obecní dům for coffee and cake. Browse luxury boutiques on Pařížská Street — Prague's equivalent of the Champs-Élysées.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar with Old Town panoramic views, followed by a premium Czech tasting dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Grand Café Orient — the world's only Cubist café, serving light Czech breakfasts in a uniquely designed interior
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá — beloved upscale Czech brasserie; try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and freshly tapped Pilsner Urquell served in traditional style
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (Michelin-starred) — the pinnacle of Czech haute cuisine; a 6 or 11-course tasting menu inspired by 19th-century Bohemian recipes, with exceptional wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Josefov admission requires a combined ticket — purchase online in advance. La Degustation requires reservations weeks ahead; book immediately. Pařížská Street is ideal for luxury shopping (Louis Vuitton, Hermès, Dior).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (1.5 hours from Prague by private car) — a UNESCO World Heritage medieval silver-mining town. Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), where 40,000 human skeletons form chandeliers and decorations. Then explore the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara, one of the finest Gothic churches in Central Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague and visit Vyšehrad — the lesser-known but deeply atmospheric fortress above the Vltava. Explore the Romanesque Rotunda of St. Martin, the neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and Paul, and the Vyšehrad Cemetery where Dvořák and Smetana are buried. Enjoy sweeping river views from the ramparts.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Prague — enjoy a farewell dinner at one of the city's most atmospheric fine-dining venues, followed by a night walk across Charles Bridge one last time.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Pivnice Dačický — a historic restaurant in a Renaissance building serving traditional Czech game dishes and local Bohemian beer
meals.dinner: Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel) — Art Deco elegance, Michelin-starred seafood and European fine dining; request a window table for atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private car for Kutná Hora trip through the hotel — approximately €120–160 round trip. The Bone Church is genuinely striking; photography is permitted. Pack the hotel luggage in the evening as tomorrow is travel day to Budapest.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Prague Main Station (Praha hlavní nádraží) for the scenic Regiojet or Czech Railways premium train to Budapest Keleti Station (approximately 6.5–7 hours). Alternatively, arrange a private luxury transfer by car (5.5 hours). Enjoy the rolling Bohemian and Slovak countryside en route. Bring a curated picnic or enjoy the dining car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest early-to-mid afternoon. Check into your luxury hotel in the heart of the city (Budapest Marriott, Four Seasons Gresham Palace, or Aria Hotel Budapest). Freshen up and take a first walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) to absorb the stunning Parliament and Buda Castle views across the river.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome evening in Budapest — explore the vibrant Great Market Hall area and take an evening stroll across the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) for illuminated views of both Buda and Pest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Prague before departure
meals.lunch: Premium dining car on the train, or a packed gourmet picnic arranged by the hotel (charcuterie, local cheeses, wine)
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown (Michelin-starred) — Budapest's premier fine-dining destination on the Danube bank; contemporary Hungarian cuisine with exceptional river views

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets or private transfer well in advance. The Four Seasons Gresham Palace is one of Europe's most spectacular hotel buildings — highly recommended. September is peak season in Budapest; all reservations must be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — take the historic funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from Clark Ádám Square. Visit the Royal Palace complex housing the Hungarian National Gallery (Baroque masterpieces and Hungarian fine art) and the Budapest History Museum. Walk to the Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) — a stunning neo-Gothic church with Zsolnay ceramic roof tiles — and the Fisherman's Bastion for the most iconic panoramic views of Budapest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross back to Pest and visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of Europe's largest and most ornate parliament buildings. Take the official guided interior tour to see the Holy Crown of Hungary, the grand staircase, and the domed hall. Afterward, explore the elegant Lipótváros (Leopold Town) neighborhood and St. Stephen's Basilica.
day_by_day.evening: Thermal bath experience at Széchenyi or Gellért Baths — a quintessential Budapest ritual. Book a private cabin and enjoy the historic Neo-Baroque pools. Follow with a refined dinner in the Jewish Quarter (VII District).

meals.breakfast: New York Café — arguably the most beautiful café in the world; a gilded neo-Baroque masterpiece serving elaborate Hungarian breakfasts and pastries
meals.lunch: Halászbástya Restaurant at Fisherman's Bastion — panoramic terrace dining with Hungarian fish soup (halászlé) and grilled river fish
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant (Michelin-starred) — located steps from the Basilica; refined Hungarian haute cuisine in a jewel-box dining room; exceptional tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at least 48 hours prior. Gellért Baths offer private VIP cabins — book through the hotel. New York Café gets very busy; arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) or book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Great Synagogue (Dohány Street Synagogue) — the largest synagogue in Europe and a deeply moving site with an attached museum and the Hungarian Jewish Memorial Garden. Continue through the VII District's ruin bars and street art scene for a fascinating contrast of history and contemporary culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) on Heroes' Square — housing one of Central Europe's finest art collections including El Greco, Raphael, and Rembrandt. Walk through the grand Millennium Monument and City Park (Városliget). Explore Vajdahunyad Castle, a fairytale architectural collage within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Danube dinner cruise — board a premium private or small-group luxury boat for a 2-hour cruise with champagne, Hungarian wines, and a curated dinner while gliding past illuminated bridges and the Parliament. One of the most romantic experiences in Europe.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most historic coffeehouse (est. 1858); try the Gerbeaud slice (layered walnut and apricot jam cake)
meals.lunch: Borkonyha WineKitchen (Michelin-starred) — outstanding Hungarian wine-focused restaurant near the Basilica; seasonal Hungarian dishes paired with natural wines
meals.dinner: Premium Danube dinner cruise with fine Hungarian cuisine — arrange through the hotel concierge (Legenda or Silver Line luxury cruises recommended)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Danube dinner cruise at least 3–4 days in advance. Borkonyha is very popular — reserve for lunch. The Great Synagogue requires a combined ticket for full access including the museum.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Central Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) for a sensory farewell: pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, salami, and handcrafted souvenirs from the upper gallery stalls. Take a final walk along the Danube Promenade and enjoy a slow coffee at a riverside café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — optional visit to the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided interior tour of one of the world's most beautiful opera houses. Alternatively, a relaxing afternoon at the hotel spa before transfer. Private chauffeur transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If the flight is late evening, enjoy a farewell dinner near the airport or back in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — leisurely final morning
meals.lunch: Stand25 Bisztró — casual yet outstanding Hungarian bistro near the Central Market Hall; try the goulash, stuffed peppers, and chimney cake (kürtőskalács)
meals.dinner: If time permits before departure: Babel Budapest — creative Hungarian fine dining in a beautifully restored historic building near the Great Synagogue

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international flight departure for Budapest airport. The Central Market Hall closes early on Sundays and is busiest on Saturday mornings. Consider pre-ordering a Tokaji Aszú wine gift set as a premium souvenir — the hotel concierge can arrange delivery to the airport.
